# Nmap

`nmap` &middot; _information-gathering_

Discovers hosts and services by probing ports on a network you are authorised to scan.

**Moderate impact.** It touches the target directly; keep the scope tight.

## What this tool needs

- A target you own or are authorised to scan (IP, hostname or CIDR).
- For SYN/host-discovery modes the runtime needs raw sockets; in WSL2 this is available but see docs/LIMITATIONS.md.

## How to use it

Pick a profile. Host discovery sends pings to find live hosts; TCP quick scan checks the 1000 most common ports; Service sends version probes; OS tries operating-system fingerprinting (unreliable through WSL2's NAT). Start small: a single host, TCP quick, then narrow down.

## Examples

```console
$ nmap -sV 192.168.1.10
$ nmap -sn 192.168.1.0/24
$ nmap -p- --min-rate 1000 192.168.1.10
```

## At a glance

- Category: `information-gathering`
- Install with: `apt install nmap`
- Baseline: yes
- Licence: NPSL (not OSI-approved; bundled with the runtime for convenience)
- Upstream: <https://nmap.org/book/man.html>
